Also keep in mind that the Ravens will still need some additional Cap space to get through the season for players that go on IR and for weekly Practice Squad elevations, so there would also need to be excess Cap space after the trade.
As the chart shows, to accommodate a trade at full price, only a Nnamdi Madubuike restructure would come close to covering Nelson’s salary, so it would likely take more than one restructure.

The chart below shows the Cap savings from the only 4 players that can be restructured for any significant amount of Cap space. As each week passes between now and the trade deadline, the Cap space created by a restructure diminishes with each passing game, since the player’s remaining salary decreases (salary is the only thing that can be converted in a restructure).
Whether it was to cover some of Nelson’s remaining salary as above or the entire amount, the Ravens quite frankly do not have a lot of great options for creating Cap space at this point.
Of course, the teams could have also agreed to some number in between, thereby leveling the trade compensation, but that would then require the Ravens to create additional Cap space on their own.

And, generally, the more a team eats in salary to make the trade work, the higher the draft pick compensation they are going to expect in return. So, that would likely have required the Ravens to offer their 2nd round pick to top the 3rd received from Seattle?

The Colts did not eat any salary in the trade with Seattle.

Given the above numbers, that would have been asking the Colts to eat as much of $8,983,333 if Nelson’s salary was reduced down to the minimum ($794,445) for the Ravens.

That left the Ravens with two options to facilitate a trade: They could have worked with the Colts (if the Colts would have been interested in doing so) to have Indy eat some of Nelson’s salary to make it easier from a Cap-perspective to make the deal happen.

Nelson is due $9,777,778M for the remaining 11 games of the season. The Ravens presently have $1,355,958 in Salary Cap space.

So, right there, you can see the first issue. Teams must have enough Cap space available when trading for a player to accommodate the salary balance.
